patches.summary: ParseSearch surfaces a real error (ErrSearchUnavailable) when Prisjakt /search returns a Cloudflare-challenged shell instead of swallowing it into an empty-but-successful listing; cross-site `lowest` now flags dropped sources via `sources_unavailable`, and the `prisjakt search` command + `prisjakt_search` MCP tool return a clear, actionable 'use PriceRunner instead' message.
patches.reason: Prisjakt moved /search to Cloudflare-challenged client-side rendering that no longer server-renders the React Query state. The old ParseSearch returned (emptyListing, nil) on parse failure, so cross-site commands (lowest, etc.) silently degraded to PriceRunner-only while still presenting as cross-site, and prisjakt_search returned an empty/null result that read as 'no matches' rather than 'search unavailable'.
patches.validated_outcome: go build/vet pass; full test suite passes including new TestParseSearchUnavailable / TestParseSearchSuccess regression tests pinning the honest-failure contract; standalone verify_skill.py passes.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Generic MCP makeAPIHandler should detect an anti-bot challenge shell / empty-shaped response and return an honest error rather than returning the raw response body as a success result. Here this required a dedicated hand-authored handler (prisjakt_search_handler.go) replacing the generated makeAPIHandler registration for prisjakt_search.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Runtime honesty for challenge-served endpoints is a generator concern: any printed CLI whose endpoint sits behind Cloudflare-CSR would exhibit the same silent empty/null result through the generic handler. Local patch is intentionally se-prices-specific until the generator learns the pattern.
